title: Content policy
description: What can't be published on he4rt ink. Every moderation decision cites a numbered item on this page.

summary.title: Respect above all
summary.text: Insults, harassment and hate speech are not accepted.

summary.title: Technical and honest content
summary.text: Cite sources and don't publish code that causes harm.

summary.title: Only what you may use
summary.text: No plagiarism and no images without usage rights.

summary.title: No disguised advertising
summary.text: Sharing your work is fine; spam isn't.

items.title: Repeated content
items.text: Publishing the same text several times, or only changing the title.
items.bad: Three identical articles with different titles.
items.good: Publishing a revised version in place of the old one.

items.title: Spam and self-promotion
items.text: Using an article, comment or username only to sell or drive traffic.
items.bad: A username like @buy-courses or an article that is just an affiliate link.
items.good: Mentioning your project or course when it's part of the technical content.

items.title: Insults and harassment
items.text: Attacking, humiliating or stalking people, on or off the platform.
items.bad: Comments that insult whoever wrote the article.
items.good: Disagreeing with the content with arguments.

items.title: Hate speech
items.text: Content that discriminates by race, gender, orientation, religion, disability or origin.
items.good: Discussing diversity and inclusion in tech.

items.title: Plagiarism
items.text: Publishing someone else's text as if it were yours.
items.bad: Translating a whole article without permission or credit.
items.good: Quoting short excerpts with the source.

items.title: Images without usage rights
items.text: Using images you didn't create and have no license to use.
items.bad: Screenshots of paid courses or stock photos without a license.
items.good: Your own images, public domain ones or ones with a license that allows the use.

items.title: Off topic
items.text: Content unrelated to technology or a career in technology.
items.bad: Recipes, party politics or chain messages.

items.title: Sources and attribution
items.text: Presenting numbers, benchmarks or technical claims without a source or a way to reproduce them.
items.bad: “Framework X is 10 times faster” without saying how it was measured.
items.good: Showing the code or the link used for the measurement.

items.title: Misleading information
items.text: Stating as fact something false that can harm people who follow the content.
items.bad: Saying an insecure configuration is the recommended one.
items.good: Giving an opinion while making clear it's an opinion.

items.title: Malicious code and third-party data
items.text: Publishing malware, credentials or other people's personal data.
items.bad: A real API token in a code example.
items.good: Explaining an already fixed vulnerability, for defense.

list: Every article is reviewed before it goes live. The decision not to approve cites the item that was broken.
Anyone with a confirmed account can report articles and comments.
Repeated or serious cases lead to suspension or ban, which you can appeal.
